title: Measuring the Eye Before Surgery

patient.name: Mr Tan Boon Seng
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for A-scan biometry before right eye cataract surgery

history.hpc: Mr Tan has been diagnosed with dense right eye cataract affecting his daily activities. He has been listed for right eye phacoemulsification. He is referred for A-scan biometry so that the correct IOL power can be calculated before surgery. He has never had eye surgery before. He currently wears reading glasses.
history.pmhx: Cataract right eye. Mild cataract left eye. Mild myopia. No previous eye surgery.
medications: Paracetamol PRN for occasional joint pain

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Dense nuclear cataract right eye. Mild cortical cataract left eye.
examination_findings.fundus: Unable to visualise right fundus due to dense cataract

diagnosis: Pre-cataract A-scan biometry completed. Axial length and keratometry values obtained. IOL power calculated for surgeon review. Right eye: 23.45mm axial length, +21.5D IOL.

immediate: Confirm correct patient identity and correct eye to be measured (check with patient and records)
Explain the A-scan procedure to the patient: painless, uses sound waves, takes about 10 minutes
Instil topical anaesthetic (proxymetacaine) if contact A-scan method is used — check if ordered
Set up A-scan machine and enter patient details correctly
Take measurements with probe aligned correctly on the centre of the cornea
Take minimum 5-10 readings per eye and record the most consistent set
Print report and document axial length, K readings, and IOL power calculation
Hand report to doctor / upload to patient record
follow_up: Surgeon to review and confirm IOL power before surgery
IOL to be ordered or selected from stock
A-scan data stored in patient's pre-operative file
patient_education: Explain that this measurement helps the surgeon choose the correct lens to implant
Tell patient the test is quick and painless
If topical anaesthetic used, advise patient not to rub eye for 30 minutes after

key_points: Confirms correct patient identity (full name and IC) and correct eye to measure
Asks about previous eye surgery (prior surgery changes axial length measurement and IOL calculation)
Asks if patient wears contact lenses — soft lenses must be removed 1 week, rigid gas-permeable 2 weeks before accurate keratometry
Explains procedure to patient before starting
Sets up A-scan machine correctly and enters patient data accurately
Takes multiple readings (minimum 5) and selects the most consistent set
Ensures probe is correctly positioned on cornea for immersion or contact method
Records axial length, corneal curvature (K readings), and IOL power calculation
Identifies purpose of A-scan: to calculate IOL power for cataract surgery
Recognises that contact lens wear affects keratometry accuracy
Identifies consistency of readings (standard deviation acceptable range)
Does not proceed with incorrect patient identity or wrong eye
Hands printed report to surgeon or uploads to records
Educates patient on the purpose of the test
Advises on contact lens removal if applicable
